source_first_reading: All nine supplied photographs were re-read and used as source guidance for a reduced, human-piloted mechanical ornithopter. The result is an educational simulation, not a claim of a recovered buildable Stanley Tinn design.

derived_geometry.calculation: Use the rounded Say span b=7.4 ft and the text's total area S=6.61 ft^2, so AR=b^2/S. The inconsistent 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is excluded.
derived_geometry.principle: Preserve broad inner arm wing, wrist at about half span, and rounded/tapered outer hand-wing planform.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Mute-swan planform proportions, AR from b^2/S, wrist-to-wrist fraction about half span, broad inner chord and tapered rounded outer wing.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: The original wing-length conversion marked around 3.135 ft is inconsistent and is not used.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Scaled to the supplied 14 m span and area=14^2/AR; source-mechanism supplies detailed panel geometry.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Section-data context only: curved-plate behaviour and ambiguous axes caution against exact coefficient recovery.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: No exact full-scale CL/CD table is claimed from the chart.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: The provided engineering.json section tables are used as illustrative assumptions.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Design method: choose trajectory, cruising speed and flapping frequency, then evaluate candidate wing actions; human-carrying mechanical flapping flight is the target.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: Historical marginal notes are not treated as design requirements.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Simulator uses the supplied masses, controls, 16 kW engine model and terrain world.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Straight and level flapping necessarily has cyclic lift/thrust and small undulating motion; powered man-carrying ornithopter context.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: The ring-vortex sketch is qualitative, not a prescribed force waveform.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Forces are computed locally from moving wing strips rather than prescribed to match a sine path.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Low-speed downstroke lasts longer than recovery; at cruise periods become equal. Wing/body/wishbone dynamics should act as a resonant mass-spring system.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Implemented theta=phi-b sin(phi), with low-speed timing bias from engineering and fixed per run.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Wing and body inertias share a common CG; fore/aft wing movement creates pitching moments; recovery closes/reduces the hand wing; tail helps align pitch.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: No numerical linkage dimensions are recovered.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: The source-mechanism helper supplies actual moving masses, CG, derivatives and coupled phase/pitch inertia.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Incidence and camber are separately adjusted during the cycle; bird-wing section figures show curved, changing sections.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: The goshawk dimensions and camber percentages are treated as examples, not swan specifications.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Camber curves are the supplied inner/outer base plus cyclic amplitude values.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Inner arm section about 5-6 percent thick; outer hand wing is a thin curved/slotted plate; trailing/partial closing on recovery reduces tip area and drag; conventional tail/rudder controls are compatible.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: Bird landing and water-ski details are not directly copied.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Two overlapping sliding outer leaves give reduced exposure on recovery; the aircraft has a tailplane, fin, rudder, elevator and three wheels.

photograph_interpretations.used_principle: Power accounting begins with D*V glide work and adds induced, trajectory, inertial, body and wing terms; springs exchange but do not create net energy.
photograph_interpretations.unreadable_or_rejected: Appendix algorithm and detailed equations are missing.
photograph_interpretations.engineering_completion: Shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, drive heat and control work are integrated from the same production forces and coupled dynamics.

visual_design: Open triangular tube fuselage, seated pilot, visible engine/crank/transmission, mast and bracing, conventional tail/fin/rudder, three actual rotating tyres, and source-mounted curved/sliding wing panels. The rendered wing surfaces are the same makePanel geometry consumed by physics through wingPose.
limitations: Engine, component masses, coefficient tables, transmission efficiency and fuel consumption are engineering assumptions, not notebook readings.
No CFD, unsteady wake, structural flexibility, aeroelastic stability proof or buildable human-flight validation is claimed.
The linkage curves are an explicit mechanical completion of the readable principles rather than digitised notebook samples.
